digest.top_line: NRG-GU005: prostate SBRT crosses DFS futility (HR 1.38, 0.91-2.09) yet beats MH-IMRT on 2-yr bowel HRQOL (35% vs 44% MCID decline).
digest.tldr: Prostate SBRT gets its first randomised head-to-head reality check: NRG-GU005 buys toxicity and bowel HRQOL, not efficacy, with 3-yr biochemical failure numerically worse (8% vs 4%), while Meier's 10-yr single-arm data show two-thirds of relapses land after year 5, so 5-yr SBRT datasets undercount failure. Head/neck gets its first ESTRO post-op CTV atlas for OCSCC.

sites.intro: Two SBRT reads pulling opposite ways (randomised HRQOL win vs efficacy futility, and a 10-yr single-arm series whose late relapses indict short follow-up), plus an ARS AUC putting biopsy and reirradiation dose schemas on the record for local recurrence.

studies.name: 10-yr SBRT for Prostate Cancer (Meier et al., Eur Urol)
studies.tldr: 10-yr RFS 92% overall, 94% LR / 86% IR, with 1.5% cumulative Gr3 GU toxicity after 40 Gy/5 fx.
details: 🔍 Phase 2 nonrandomized multi-institutional trial, N=310 evaluable (172 LR, 138 IR), 21 community/regional/academic sites, accrual Jan 2008 to Apr 2010
🔍 40 Gy in 5 fractions (8 Gy × 5, ~100 Gy EQD2 at α/β=2) on a noncoplanar robotic platform; fiducial tracking + translational and rotational intrafractional correction mandatory
🔍 Androgen suppression not allowed, so the RFS signal is RT-attributable rather than ADT-confounded
🔍 Eligibility LR (T1b-T2a, Gleason 6, PSA ≤10) or IR (T1b-T2b, Gleason 7 or Gleason 6 with PSA 10-20), central path review; prostate volume up to 100 cc, no TURP or AUA-score exclusion

details.text: 📊 10-yr outcomes by risk group (Kaplan-Meier, median f/u 9 yr)

details: 📊 MSK favorable vs unfavorable IR 10-yr RFS 92% (90-100) vs 77% (60-93), p=0.002; the only split that separated
📊 Grade 2+ toxicity at 10 yr: GI 2.1%, GU 14%; four pts had five grade 3 events, all GU, none after year 5, no grade 4-5
🔗 vs RTOG 0126 dose-escalated EBRT: IR 10-yr RFS 86% here vs 74-78% reported there, per the authors' own comparison
🔗 vs PACE-B and PATRIOT: toxicity higher in those SBRT arms; PACE-B reported several-fold higher CTCAE rates on conventional linac vs the 41% treated with CyberKnife, consistent with MIRAGE
⚠️ Nonrandomized single-arm; the EBRT comparison is cross-trial and historical, and the authors state a randomized trial is required for meaningful comparison
⚠️ Sponsor-funded (Accuray) with a device-specific platform and mandatory intrafractional tracking; the toxicity result may not transfer to linac-based SBRT
⚠️ Two-thirds of relapses occurred between 5 and 10 yr, so 5-yr datasets (including PACE-B) systematically undercount failure

verdict.rationale: Single-arm nonrandomized phase 2; EBRT comparison is cross-trial historical. Sponsor-funded, single-platform. Extends duration of existing SBRT evidence rather than establishing superiority.
verdict.audience: Organ-confined low- or intermediate-risk prostate, no ADT, prostate ≤100 cc

studies.significance: Two-thirds of relapses fell between 5 and 10 yr, so the 5-yr PACE-B read undercounts failure and this is the first 10-yr prospective SBRT dataset. Grade group 3 was the only independent predictor of 10-yr failure, and unfavorable IR sat at 77% RFS, which is where the ADT-addition question actually lives.
studies.monday_clinic: In favorable intermediate- or low-risk organ-confined disease, this supports 40 Gy/5 fx monotherapy without ADT out to 10 yr; it does not resolve grade group 3 unfavorable IR, where 10-yr RFS was 77%.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Investigator-initiated **phase 2 nonrandomized** trial across **21 centers** (community, regional, academic), treated January 2008 to April 2010, **N=310 evaluable**. Median follow-up **9 yr**; Kaplan-Meier with day 0 at last day of treatment, log-rank between LR and IR.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **172 low-risk** (T1b-T2a, Gleason 6, PSA ≤10) and **138 intermediate-risk** (T1b-T2b, Gleason 7, or Gleason 6 with PSA 10-20), median age **68**, central pathologic review. IR subcategorized favorable vs unfavorable by MSK criteria. Prostate volume up to **100 cc** eligible; prior TURP and baseline AUA symptom score were **not exclusions**.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **40 Gy in 5 fractions** (8 Gy × 5, equivalent to ~100 Gy at 2 Gy/fx assuming α/β=2), noncoplanar robotic platform with real-time motion management. **Fiducial tracking plus translational and rotational intrafractional correction were mandatory**. **Adjuvant hormone therapy was not allowed**.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Relapse defined as biochemical failure (**nadir+2**), clinical failure, or administration of any salvage, antiandrogen or systemic therapy. Late toxicity was physician-reported, **CTCAE v3**, events after 3 mo.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Ten-yr cumulative **grade 3 GI or GU 1.4% (LR) and 1.5% (IR)**, far below the prespecified 10% rate, with **no grade 4-5 events** and **no new grade 3+ events after year 5**. Grade 2+ at 10 yr was **GI 2.1%** and **GU 14%**; all five grade 3 events (in four pts) were GU.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: IR 10-yr RFS **86%** compares against **74-78%** with dose-escalated EBRT in **RTOG 0126**. Toxicity was similar to Fuller's CyberKnife trial but lower than the **PACE-B** SBRT arm and **PATRIOT**, both linac-weighted; PACE-B reported several-fold higher CTCAE toxicity on conventional linac vs the 41% treated with CyberKnife.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents organ-confined low- and favorable-intermediate-risk prostate cancer treated with robotic SBRT without ADT. Does not represent high-risk, node-positive, or post-prostatectomy disease, nor linac-based delivery without intrafractional rotational tracking.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Accrual closed in 2010, so staging predates MRI and PSMA PET and the cohort is stage-migration-naive relative to today's IR patients. Toxicity is physician-reported CTCAE v3 with no patient-reported instrument, which understates GU bother, and the platform requirement (mandatory rotational intrafractional correction, Accuray-funded) makes the toxicity result device-conditional.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The authors' multivariate analysis found **grade group 3** the only unfavorable risk factor independently predicting 10-yr biochemical/clinical failure, which they frame as an argument for considering ADT in that subgroup. They also note **two-thirds of relapses occurred between 5 and 10 yr**, mirroring Fuller's SBRT trial.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The transferability gate is the platform, not the dose: 40 Gy/5 fx is standard, but mandatory fiducial plus rotational intrafractional correction is what separates this 1.5% grade 3 rate from the higher PACE-B and PATRIOT linac-weighted rates. Unfavorable IR at 77% RFS, driven by grade group 3, is where ADT addition remains open.

open_questions: Does ADT addition improve outcomes in unfavorable intermediate-risk grade group 3?
Does robotic tracking reduce late toxicity vs linac-based prostate SBRT?
Do PACE-B relapse rates diverge from EBRT beyond 5 yr?

studies.name: American Radium Society AUC: Local Intraprostatic Recurrence
studies.tldr: ARS AUC: biopsy mandatory before salvage, reirradiation usually appropriate, ADT alone not recommended, short ADT only with salvage RT.
details: 🔍 Modified Delphi, 12 voting members (rad onc, urology, med onc), 2 voting rounds, RAND disagreement methodology
🔍 PRISMA search of PubMed + Embase run 28 June 2022 across 4 topics; conference abstracts and <5-pt series excluded

rows: PSMA PET + mpMRI both recommended; biopsy always required before local salvage
Strong consensus for BOTH systematic and targeted biopsies
Reirradiation usually appropriate; cryotherapy or HIFU may be appropriate; ADT alone not recommended
Short course probably appropriate with salvage SBRT; long courses recommended against
Focal if mpMRI + systematic biopsy agree on location; whole-gland if they disagree

details.text: 📐 Reirradiation dose schemas the panel considers acceptable
subdetails: SBRT 34-40 Gy in 5 fx (34 Gy/5 fx Fuller prospective series, n=50; 40 Gy/5 fx focal MTD in NCI dose-finding)
EBRT 36 Gy in 6 fx (GETUG-AFU 31 phase 1/2, focal, GTV by mpMRI + choline PET, 5-7mm CTV margin)
HDR 27 Gy in 2 fx, 32 Gy in 4 fx (single insertion, 30h), or 36 Gy in 6 fx over 2 implants
LDR 140 Gy (I-125) or 120 Gy (Pd-103), per RTOG 0526

details.text: 📊 MASTER meta-analysis (150 studies, 11 322 pts): adjusted severe toxicity vs RP

details: 📊 MASTER adjusted 5-yr RFS 50-60% across modalities, no significant survival difference vs RP
📊 RTOG 0526 (salvage LDR, n=92): DFS 61% at 5 yr, 33% at 10 yr, 10-yr local failure 5%, median f/u 6.7 yr
🔍 FORECAST: mpMRI sens 94% (88-98%), spec 18% (7-35%); MRI-targeted biopsy sens 92% (83-97%), spec 75% (45-92%)
🔗 Liu et al (n=79 exclusively radiorecurrent): PSMA PET vs conventional concordant in 56%, 34% upstaged, 10% downstaged
⚠️ Evidence base predates PSMA PET, so the exact population the guideline targets was not identifiable in the source studies
⚠️ Data limited to pts initially treated with conventionally fractionated EBRT; prior brachytherapy excluded, and moderate/ultrahypofractionation is now SOC
⚠️ Panel disagreement on castrate-resistant local recurrence (variant 3), second salvage (variant 4), and prior grade 3 toxicity (variant 5)
⚠️ No agreement on relugolix in the radiorecurrent setting; HERO MACE signal was an unplanned secondary analysis and PRONOUNCE did not replicate
⚠️ Topics 3 and 4 had no studies meeting inclusion criteria, so those recommendations are expert opinion only

verdict.rationale: ARS appropriate use criteria, modified Delphi of 12 panelists. Output is an appropriateness allocation, not an outcome; topics 3 and 4 had no qualifying evidence.
verdict.audience: Biopsy-confirmed isolated intraprostatic recurrence after definitive EBRT

studies.significance: The panel puts the reirradiation decision on a defined menu (34-40 Gy/5 fx SBRT, 36 Gy/6 fx, HDR 27 Gy/2 fx, LDR 140 Gy I-125) and gates focal vs whole-gland on mpMRI-biopsy concordance, not on lesion size. It also makes tissue mandatory: PSMA PET alone is not enough to reirradiate.
studies.monday_clinic: In a man with rising PSA after definitive EBRT and PSMA PET showing prostate-only avidity, this supports systematic plus targeted biopsy before any salvage and favors reirradiation over ADT alone; it does not extend to nodal or metastatic recurrence, prior brachytherapy, or recurrence after hypofractionated primary RT.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: ARS Genitourinary Appropriate Use Criteria: PRISMA literature search (PubMed + Embase, 28 June 2022) feeding evidence tables, then **modified Delphi** voting by a **12-member** multidisciplinary panel over **two rounds**, with RAND methodology to separate true disagreement from misread variants.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Scope is **tier A only**: isolated intraprostatic radiorecurrence after definitive RT, with nodal (tier B) and distant (tier C) failure excluded. All variants presuppose a patient who **desires curative-intent local salvage**. Evidence is restricted to pts initially treated with conventionally fractionated EBRT; **prior brachytherapy was excluded**.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Acceptable reirradiation schemas: **SBRT 34-40 Gy in 5 fx**, EBRT **36 Gy in 6 fx** (GETUG-AFU 31), HDR **27 Gy in 2 fx** / 32 Gy in 4 fx / 36 Gy in 6 fx over two implants, LDR **140 Gy (I-125) or 120 Gy (Pd-103)** per RTOG 0526. Most regimens deliver in **six or fewer fractions**. GETUG-AFU 31 defines GTV by mpMRI plus choline PET with a **5-7 mm CTV margin** bound by the capsule.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Recommendations rather than effect sizes: biopsy (systematic **and** targeted) is required before salvage, reirradiation is **usually appropriate**, cryotherapy and HIFU **may be appropriate**, and **ADT alone is not recommended**. A short **4-6 mo LHRH agonist** course is probably appropriate concurrent with salvage SBRT in pts without cardiac history.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: The toxicity argument rests on MASTER (150 studies, **11 322 pts**): adjusted severe GU **20% after RP vs 5.6% SBRT, 9.6% HDR, 9.1% LDR**, and severe GI **1.8% RP vs 0.0% HDR (p < 0.01)**. RTOG 0526 adds prospective LDR support with **10-yr local failure 5%**.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents biopsy-confirmed isolated intraprostatic recurrence after conventionally fractionated definitive EBRT. Does not represent nodal or metastatic recurrence, prior brachytherapy, or recurrence after moderate/ultrahypofractionated primary RT.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Topics 3 (hormonal therapy with salvage) and 4 (focal vs whole-gland) had **no studies meeting inclusion criteria**, so those recommendations are pure panel opinion. Variants 3-5 (castrate-resistant local recurrence, second salvage, prior grade 3 toxicity) ended in **explicit disagreement**, and the search cutoff of June 2022 leaves a documented lag to publication.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The practical shift is diagnostic: PSMA PET upstaged **34%** and downstaged **10%** of radiorecurrent men (Liu, n=79), yet Fendler reported an **8% false-positive rate** driven largely by post-RT change, which is why the panel makes tissue mandatory rather than treating on imaging. FORECAST's secondary analysis found up to **59%** of true radiorecurrences would be occult on targeted biopsy alone.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Reirradiation is the panel's preferred salvage, with a defined menu (34-40 Gy/5 fx SBRT, 36 Gy/6 fx, HDR 27 Gy/2 fx, LDR 140 Gy I-125) and a concordance rule for volume: focal when mpMRI and systematic biopsy agree, whole-gland when they do not. Adjusted severe GU was 5.6% after SBRT vs 20% after RP.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: ADT alone is recommended against for confirmed local recurrence, irrespective of agent or duration; the only endorsed hormonal role is a short 4-6 mo LHRH agonist for radiosensitization with salvage RT. Classic ADT is preferred over novel agents, and the panel reached no agreement on relugolix given HERO's unplanned secondary MACE analysis and PRONOUNCE's null result.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Salvage RP remains an option with no significant survival difference vs other modalities in MASTER, but it carries the worst adjusted severe toxicity (GU 20% vs 5.6-9.6% for salvage RT, GI 1.8% vs 0.0% HDR). Biopsy is required first, and combined biopsy-plus-ablation approaches are discouraged.

open_questions: Salvage safety after upfront moderate or ultrahypofractionated RT
Focal vs whole-gland salvage in the PSMA PET era
Optimal management of castrate-resistant local intraprostatic recurrence

studies.name: NRG-GU005
studies.tldr: DFS futility crossed (HR 1.38, 95% CI 0.91-2.09, p=0.13); SBRT not superior to MH-IMRT, but bowel HRQOL better.

details.text: 🔍 Randomized non-blinded phase III, N=698 (SBRT 353, MH-IMRT 345), co-primary DFS + EPIC-26 HRQOL

details: 🔍 SBRT 36.25 Gy/5 fx (7.25 Gy, 2-3 fx/wk), CTV-PTV 5 mm radial, 3 mm posterior + anterior
🔍 MH-IMRT 70 Gy/28 fx or 60 Gy/20 fx, CTV-PTV 8 mm except 5 mm posterior
🔍 CTV = prostate ± 1 cm proximal SV; fiducials, MRI fusion and daily IGRT mandated
📊 PTV max dose capped 38.78 Gy without urethral visualization; acceptable variation 43.5 Gy

details.text: 📊 EPIC-26 MCID decline rates, SBRT vs MH-IMRT
📐 Longitudinal mixed-model treatment effect (least square mean, favors SBRT)
subdetails: Bowel domain: LS mean 2.68 (95% CI 1.02, 4.34), p=0.0016
Urinary incontinence: LS mean 2.91 (95% CI 0.85, 4.97), p=0.0058
Sexual and hormonal domains: no significant treatment effect

details: ⚠️ 3-yr cumulative biochemical failure higher with SBRT: 8% (5.2-11.0) vs 4% (2.3-7.0), p=0.037
⚠️ DFS point estimate favors IMRT numerically; 5-yr DFS 89% (85-92) SBRT vs 92% (89-95) IMRT
🔗 vs PACE-B: both trials show lower urinary incontinence decline with SBRT, though MCID definitions differ

details.text: ⚠️ Rectal spacer used in 56% SBRT vs 55% IMRT and independently improved bowel scores (LS mean -2.81, 95% CI -4.49, -1.13; p=0.0011), confounding the bowel read

verdict.rationale: Randomized phase III, but efficacy co-primary stopped at interim futility; toxicity co-primary partially met. Supports SBRT as an option, does not establish superiority.
verdict.audience: Localized intermediate-risk prostate cancer, median age 68, RT-eligible

studies.significance: The bowel HRQOL win is confounded: rectal spacer, used in 56% SBRT vs 55% IMRT, independently improved bowel scores (LS mean -2.81, p=0.0011). The harder number for an RT reader is 3-yr biochemical failure, 8% vs 4% (p=0.037) against 36.25 Gy/5 fx, which argues against treating five fractions as dose-equivalent in intermediate risk.
studies.monday_clinic: In localized intermediate-risk prostate cancer choosing between five-fraction SBRT and moderate hypofractionation, this supports SBRT on bowel and incontinence HRQOL and investigator-reported toxicity while flagging a higher early biochemical failure rate; it does not speak to high-risk disease, nodal coverage, or SBRT with ADT.

primary_endpoint.name: Disease-free survival (co-primary)
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: 95% CI 0.91-2.09, p=0.13; futility bound crossed, not superior

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Randomized, non-blinded, international **phase III**, 1:1, **N=698** (SBRT 353, MH-IMRT 345), 2 ineligible. Stratified by Gleason score, PSA, and rectal manipulation (balloon or hydrogel spacer). Both co-primary endpoints had interim futility analyses.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Localized **intermediate-risk** prostate cancer, median age 68 (IMRT) and 69 (SBRT), range 42-84. Rectal manipulation used in ~59% overall (SpaceOAR 55%). Baseline EPIC-26 domain scores balanced across arms (all p>0.09).

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **SBRT 36.25 Gy in 5 fractions** of 7.25 Gy at 2-3 fractions/week, CTV-PTV 5 mm radial and 3 mm posterior/anterior. **MH-IMRT 70 Gy/28 fx or 60 Gy/20 fx**, CTV-PTV 8 mm except 5 mm posteriorly. CTV = prostate ± 1 cm proximal seminal vesicles; fiducials, MRI fusion, and daily advanced IGRT mandated.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Co-primary:** superiority of SBRT for (1) EPIC-26 bowel and urinary irritative/obstructive MCID decline at 24 months, powered for 10% and 8% absolute reductions; (2) DFS (Phoenix biochemical failure, local, regional, distant failure, or death), powered for HR 0.62, 178 events from 590 evaluable.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: DFS futility bound crossed at interim: **HR 1.38 (0.91-2.09), p=0.13**, 5-yr DFS 89% (85-92) SBRT vs 92% (89-95) IMRT. 5-yr OS 91% (85-95) vs 94% (90-97), p=0.66. Bowel MCID decline **35% vs 44%, p=0.034**; urinary irritative/obstructive **35% vs 34%, p=0.68**.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Investigator-reported toxicity favored SBRT: treatment-related **G3+ GU 0.6% vs 2.5% (p=0.04)**, any-grade rectal hemorrhage 10.5% vs 17.3% (p=0.01), any-grade fatigue 39.2% vs 50.8% (p=0.0025).

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: PACE-B is the other large SBRT vs MH-IMRT randomized comparison; both trials show lower urinary incontinence decline with SBRT despite differing MCID definitions. MH-IMRT's standing rests on RTOG 0415 and its long-term analysis.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents localized intermediate-risk prostate cancer treated with prostate-only RT and daily IGRT, over half with a rectal spacer. Does not represent high-risk or node-positive disease, elective nodal coverage, or RT with ADT.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Non-blinded with patient-reported co-primary endpoints, so response bias runs toward the arm with fewer visits. Rectal spacer, a stratification factor used in over half the cohort, independently improved bowel scores (LS mean -2.81, p=0.0011), which sits directly on the positive bowel co-primary. EPIC completion was ~82-84%, and the higher SBRT biochemical failure rate is a 3-yr cumulative incidence, not a mature endpoint.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The trial answers the convenience question rather than the efficacy question: five fractions buys a bowel and incontinence HRQOL advantage and lower investigator-reported toxicity, at no demonstrated disease-control gain and an early biochemical failure signal running the wrong way. Whether that signal converts to clinical failure needs the mature DFS read.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Two numbers gate the fractionation choice. The bowel HRQOL win is confounded by rectal spacer (56% SBRT vs 55% IMRT), which independently improved bowel scores (LS mean -2.81, p=0.0011). Against that, 3-yr biochemical failure was 8% vs 4% (p=0.037), so 36.25 Gy/5 fx should not be assumed dose-equivalent.

open_questions: Does the early biochemical failure signal mature into clinical failure
Is 36.25 Gy in 5 fractions biologically adequate for intermediate risk
How much of the bowel HRQOL benefit is spacer-driven

sites.intro: First ESTRO consensus CTV atlas for post-op OCSCC, filling a gap where no delineation guideline existed.

studies.name: ESTRO Post-op CTV Delineation Guidelines (Oral Cavity SCC)
studies.tldr: First ESTRO post-op CTV atlas for OCSCC: CTV-P = (GTV-P pre-op + 10 mm) ∪ (surgical defect/flap + 5 mm), EQD2 60 Gy.
details: 🔍 ESTRO multidisciplinary expert group; no prior consensus guideline existed for post-op CTV in mucosal HNSCC

details.text: 📐 CTV-P composite: GTV-P pre-op + 10 mm isotropic, plus surgical defect or flap + 5 mm isotropic, edited for bone, fascia, air, teeth, intra-oral prosthesis
🔍 10 mm around GTV-P pre-op mirrors the 5 + 5 mm definitive-setting expansion; grounded in surgical series showing microscopic infiltration within 5 mm of GTV-P edge in >95 % of resected OCSCC
📊 Nodal CTV margin around the re-created GTV-N pre-op depends on pENE
subdetails: No pENE: GTV-N pre-op + 5 mm, composited with involved level(s) and post-op change → CTV-N1
pENE present: GTV-N pre-op + 10 mm → CTV-N high-risk, for radial spread from a disrupted capsule
Nodes not identifiable on pre-op imaging or poor co-registration: delineate whole involved level(s) + seroma/clips instead

details.text: 🔍 Neck PORT thresholds after neck dissection
subdetails: pN0 after adequate (≥18 node) dissection: neck PORT generally not required
pN1 after adequate dissection: PORT may not be required; single node >10 mm but ≤30 mm is 'intermediate risk'
Single node ≤10 mm: adjuvant RT not routinely recommended
pN2-N3: neck PORT required, CTV-N1 plus adjacent and undissected at-risk levels

details: 🔍 Rigid co-registration of pre-op contrast CT and/or MRI to a 2.0 mm (range 1–3 mm) planning CT, matched to C1-C3 or mandible/maxilla, not to soft tissue
🔗 Extends the 2018 definitive-setting HNSCC CTV guidelines and complements GORTEC 2020 flap delineation, which outlined flap body and vascular pedicle separately
⚠️ Consensus by expert discussion and international peer review, not a scored Delphi; no agreement statistics reported in source
⚠️ Dose to dissected uninvolved levels is explicitly unresolved; the supporting MD Anderson observation dates to 1993 and was never tested prospectively
⚠️ Reduced-dose flap-core approaches are described but not recommended: the guideline states a lack of data and consensus on their value
⚠️ Scope is OCSCC only; R2 resection is excluded, and other head-and-neck subsites are deferred to future guidelines

verdict.rationale: ESTRO expert guideline, not a trial. Output is a delineation method and dose allocation; no efficacy endpoint, no comparative outcome data, no scored agreement metric reported.
verdict.audience: Resected oral cavity SCC referred for PORT, any margin status; R2 excluded

studies.significance: The operational change is delineating a surrogate GTV-P pre-op alongside the defect or flap, not the flap alone: Fig 3.1 shows a buccal case where the re-created GTV-P extended superiorly beyond the defect and a flap-only CTV would have geographically missed the infratemporal fossa. Same logic nodally, where GTV-N pre-op + 10 mm covers pENE spread that level-based landmarks undercover caudally.
studies.monday_clinic: In a resected OCSCC patient with a flap reconstruction and adverse pathology, this supports building CTV-P from both the re-created pre-op GTV and the flap rather than the flap alone; it does not address R2 resections or non-oral-cavity subsites.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: ESTRO-convened multidisciplinary expert group; guidelines developed by discussion and review of current evidence and international practice, then **reviewed by HNSCC experts from countries outside the authorship** (Japan, Hong Kong, Australia, Brazil, Mexico, Canada, Denmark, France, Spain, Poland, Ireland, UK) and modified on that feedback. **No voting or agreement statistics are reported.**

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma requiring **post-operative radiotherapy**, applied **regardless of margin status and other histological risk factors**. **R2 resection (macroscopic residual disease) is explicitly out of scope.**

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Planning CT **2.0 mm slices (range 1–3 mm)** skull base to below the sterno-clavicular joint with mandatory IV contrast, rigidly co-registered to pre-op MRI or CT and matched to **C1-C3 or adjacent bone**, not soft tissue. **CTV-P = (GTV-P pre-op + 10 mm) + (surgical defect or flap + 5 mm)**, edited for bone, fascia, air, teeth and any intra-oral prosthesis. Nodally, **GTV-N pre-op + 5 mm** without pENE and **+ 10 mm** with pENE.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: No clinical endpoint. The deliverable is a **step-by-step delineation method** (Table 1), a **nodal-level allocation table by pN category and laterality** (Table 2), and worked example cases across oral tongue, buccal mucosa, floor of mouth, retromolar trigone and mandibular alveolus with defect, RFFF, nasolabial, buccal fat pad, fibula and pectoralis major reconstructions.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Dose allocation is the actionable output: **CTV-P and CTV-N1 EQD2 60 Gy**, **CTV-N2 50 Gy**, **high-risk volumes (positive <1 mm margin or pENE) 64–66 Gy**. For a positive margin that can be localised, the high-dose volume may be either the whole CTV-P or a **10 mm thick strip lying 5 mm each side of the flap-native tissue interface**.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents resected OCSCC of any subsite proceeding to PORT, including flap-reconstructed necks. Does not represent R2 resections, non-oral-cavity head and neck subsites, or definitive (non-operative) radiotherapy.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The dose to dissected but uninvolved levels rests on a **1993 MD Anderson observation never tested prospectively**, and the guideline concedes practice variation there. Flap-core dose reduction is described without endorsement for **lack of data and consensus**. Validation is deferred: the authors ask for prospective audits of practice and outcomes to establish these volumes as standard of care.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The geometric-margin rationale carries external support: DAHANCA showed geometric expansion is more conformal than anatomical margins, and a **post-hoc De-ESCALaTE analysis correlated the anatomical-to-geometric protocol change with lower late dysphagia**. Dutch non-randomised series reducing the high-risk margin from **10 mm to 6 mm** reported lower salivary and constrictor dose with less acute and late toxicity, which puts the 10 mm post-op margin chosen here on the conservative side of an actively moving question.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Delineate a surrogate GTV-P pre-op, not the flap alone: Fig 3.1's buccal case had the re-created GTV-P extend superiorly past the defect, and a flap-only CTV would have missed the infratemporal fossa. Nodally, GTV-N pre-op + 10 mm covers pENE spread that level-based landmarks undercover caudally.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: The volumes are built from operative and pathology detail, so defect versus flap body, pedicle course, marrow-space invasion and the anatomic site of a <1 mm margin all change what gets 60 versus 64–66 Gy. A surgical clip at a positive deep margin let one case take a focal high-dose strip instead of the whole CTV-P. Adequate dissection is defined as ≥18 nodes.
